thread:
sara_support: 🚨 Support pile-in: multiple customers reporting 502/504s and timeouts hitting the hosted inference API since ~15:03 UTC. High severity.

sara_support: examples from tickets: 
- customer A: repeated 502s during generation; trace id f2a3b9
- customer B: timeouts on /v1/generate, RTT spikes then 504s

sara_support: cc @mike_oncall @kevin_runtime — can you triage? I collected basic logs and one curl repro.

mike_oncall: looking. Any release or config change around 15:00?

lee_prod: yes, we started a staged configuration swap for "binary_prefetch": enabled for canary group at 14:57, targeting 20% traffic.

kevin_runtime: noted. That flag touches request prefetching + KV-cache warming path. Could cause head-of-line blocking if prefetch spawns long upstream requests.

ashley_sre: observability shows a jump in 5xx rate at 15:02 from ~0.3% to 6.8% on api-router. Downstream workers show connection resets to runtime pool.

observability-bot: alert: api-router 5xx rate > 5% for 3m. P95 latency increased from 120ms -> 1.6s. Top error class: upstream: connection_reset / upstream_timeout.

mike_oncall: can you paste the deploy/change id?

lee_prod: change_id: cfg-2026-03-17-1023, operator: @lee_prod. Canary targets: route-tag prefetched=true (20%) on us-west-2.

kevin_runtime: quick sanity check — run a sample curl against a failing trace id. Could be kernel-level backlog in runtime.

julia_csm: customers are asking for ETA. Two enterprise tenants are impacted. Please advise fast.

mike_oncall: asked ops to pause the canary rollout. @deploy-bot, pause rollout cfg-2026-03-17-1023

deploy-bot: command accepted. Pausing staged swap for cfg-2026-03-17-1023. Active canary remains at current percent until rollback/undo.

kevin_runtime: checking worker logs. Snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T15:03:11Z] WARN runtime: prefetch: spawn error: upstream connection timeout
[2026-03-17T15:03:12Z] ERROR router: upstream reset; pool=runtime-20; active=64; queued=320
[2026-03-17T15:03:12Z] ERROR http: respond 502 trace=f2a3b9
```
kevin_runtime: seeing large growth in queued requests per worker after prefetch enabled. Looks like prefetch is issuing extra upstream queries that saturate runtime connections and cause connection reset/rejects.

ashley_sre: suggestion: reduce canary to 0 or rollback flag immediately while we investigate. If we reduce canary traffic we'll stop the wave.

mike_oncall: agree. @deploy-bot, rollback cfg-2026-03-17-1023 to previous config (binary_prefetch=false) across canary targets.
deploy-bot: initiating rollback for cfg-2026-03-17-1023 -> previous. Triggering config push to api-router and runtime pools.

observability-bot: note: starting automated mitigation: route fallback to stable variant for 20% of traffic.

kevin_runtime: after rollback command I see a drop in queued counts within ~60s on a few workers. Watching 5xx rate now.

ashley_sre: 15:06 UTC: 5xx rate down to 1.1%, p95 latency returning towards baseline.

mike_oncall: good. Requesting logs for the canary hosts to correlate exact failure mode. Any evidence of OOM or thread exhaustion?

kevin_runtime: no OOM. It's connection pool starvation; the prefetch path opened synchronous upstream calls without respecting pool limits. Fix is to make prefetch asynchronous or bound by pool tokens.

lee_prod: we'll revert the change permanently for now and create a safer rollout plan (gradual increase, pool token gating).

julia_csm: communicating to customers: we'll send an incident update to impacted tenants with root cause summary and mitigation ETA.

mike_oncall: support, please collect the ticket IDs and affected accounts so SRE can confirm full recovery per tenant.

sara_support: collected and posted list to #support-escalations. Notifying the two enterprise customers now.

mike_oncall: next steps: 1) ship hotfix to guard prefetch with pool tokens OR make it background; 2) add a canary health check to detect upstream queueing spikes; 3) postmortem. Assigning to kevin_runtime + ashley_sre.

kevin_runtime: will open an internal PR with tests to stub upstream calls and ensure bounded concurrency.

ashley_sre: I'll add alert playbook notes: when config swap touches prefetch/KV, autoscale or pause canary if queued>200 for >2m.

deploy-bot: rollback completed at 15:08:30 UTC. Change cfg-2026-03-17-1023 reverted.

observability-bot: follow-up: 15:10 UTC 5xx rate < 0.5%, latency back to baseline.

mike_oncall: thanks team. Julia/support please send update. We'll track postmortem and action items in the incident tracker. :thumbsup:

julia_csm: update sent to customers 15:18 UTC. They appreciated quick rollback. We'll share the postmortem when ready.

sara_support: closing thread on support side pending postmortem. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
